text: The first night falls on a city with no one in it. For now, the lights still burn.
Power stations can run on their own for a while. But with no one to feed them fuel, or fix a single fault, the grid starts to break apart.
One by one, the lights go out.
Within a day, most of the city is dark. Freezers thaw. Phones die. The internet goes silent.
Deep below the streets, the pumps that kept the water out have stopped.
Without them, many metro tunnels would flood in just a couple of days.
By the end of the first week, the pets left behind are on their own.
Hungry dogs form packs, and roam the empty streets in search of food.
One month in, the city is still standing. But it no longer belongs to us.
Because something else is already moving in.
